_info.comment: The difficulty bomb across the schedule: growing, then frozen, then gone, at THIS CHAIN'S REAL ACTIVATION HEIGHTS. The interval is held at 9 seconds, which every rule through Mystique treats identically, so the whole visible spread between labels is the bomb. Through Gas Reprice it grows unchecked. From Die Hard ECIP-1010 freezes the explosion clause's reference point at block 3,000,000 and holds it there until 5,000,000, then resumes with the two-million-block span subtracted -- so the curve is FLAT across the window and CONTINUOUS at the resume. Gotham changes emission and not difficulty, so its expectations must equal Die Hard's, and that equality is an assertion rather than redundancy. From Defuse, ECIP-1041 removes the clause entirely, and it returns before the clause is reached, which is why the pause schedule becomes unobservable rather than merely unused.
_info.whyTheHeightsAreREALAndNoLongerRebased: REPLACES A FIXTURE THAT MEASURED NOTHING, and the failure is worth keeping because it is not obvious. The previous version rebased every label's activation heights to zero, so ECIP-1010's pause ran from block 0 to block 2,000,000. With a pause block of ZERO, 'freeze the reference during the window' and 'subtract the span, floored at zero' are THE SAME FUNCTION -- so the rule collapsed into a plain bomb delay, which is a thing this chain does not have. Measured rather than reasoned: a build implementing neither ECIP-1010 nor ECIP-1041 scored 264 of 264 on the published cases, and so did a build substituting a large delay for the removal. The suite reported success and could not distinguish a correct client from one carrying neither of the two proposals the file is named for. Worse than a coverage gap: a delay-of-2,000,000 build passes, and that build computes the WRONG difficulty on mainnet at every height between 3,000,000 and 5,000,000. A fixture a wrong implementation passes teaches the wrong rule. The pause's identity is only visible where the pause block is non-zero, so the heights are now this chain's own.
_info.whatALabelSELECTS: A label says WHICH of this chain's difficulty rules are present; each present rule is then evaluated at currentBlockNumber using its REAL mainnet parameter. That is the shape of the production client's own clause, where every branch is an IsEnabled(getter, next) test against one configuration -- so a label here is that configuration with the transitions it does not yet carry set to nil. Concretely: Frontier, Homestead and Gas Reprice carry the plain clause and neither ECIP; Die Hard and Gotham add ECIP-1010 with its pause at 3,000,000; Defuse and everything after add ECIP-1041 at 5,900,000 on top of it. Two consequences a reader should expect rather than treat as errors. Below 3,000,000 EVERY label agrees, because no rule has anything to say there yet, and that agreement is an assertion. And the removing labels still carry a bomb below 5,900,000 -- removal has its own activation height like every other rule, so it is asserted at its boundary rather than declared for the whole label. THE PREVIOUS VERSION DECLARED IT: it wrote zero at every height under those labels, which is why nothing in it could tell removal from a delay large enough to floor out at the heights it sampled.
_info.howTheDiscriminatorsWork: Three heights inside the pause window -- 3,100,000, 4,000,000 and 4,999,999 -- all carry the SAME bomb, because the reference is frozen. No delay of any size makes 2**((n-D)//100000 - 2) constant across three heights spanning 1.9 million blocks, so a delay model cannot satisfy them however it is tuned. The pause block itself is included and deliberately does NOT discriminate: there the frozen reference equals the height, so paused and plain labels coincide, and a fixture built only from the boundary would have proved nothing. REMOVAL is pinned differently, and the difference matters. No finite set of heights can separate removal from an arbitrarily large delay if all you sample is heights where both give zero -- which is what the previous version did, and why any delay above its sample range passed. What separates them is a PAIR ACROSS THE BOUNDARY: at 5,899,999 the removing labels must still carry a bomb, and at 5,900,000 they must carry none. A delay produces zero on BOTH sides or on neither, so no delay of any size satisfies the pair. Measured: with the pair in place, every wrong build tested fails, including one with a delay of 10**9, and the best of them reaches 321 of 384 where all of them previously reached 264 of 264.
_info.oracle: Two independent implementations, read line by line rather than run, because the generator that produced the previous values cannot be configured for these heights. core-geth production v1.12.21-unstable at commit 4185df450 -- consensus.go's explosion clause with consensus_classic.go's ecip1010Explosion -- expresses the rule as a reference point frozen at the pause block and then reduced by the window's length. This project's Nethermind overlay, DifficultyBombCalculator.cs, expresses the same rule as a FIXED PERIOD during the window and a PERIOD DELAY after it, with no reference point anywhere in it. The two decompositions were transcribed separately and agree at all 612 heights probed across 0 to 6,000,000 including every boundary. A control confirms the comparison discriminates: the rebased model this fixture replaces disagrees with both at 486 of those 612 heights. Agreement across a representational difference, not between two copies of one computation.
_info.oracle-version: core-geth v1.12.21-unstable @ 4185df450; Nethermind ETC overlay, read 2026-08-24
_info.ecip1010: pause 3,000,000, continue 5,000,000, span 2,000,000 -- read from ClassicChainConfig's ECIP1010PauseBlock and ECIP1010Length
_info.ecip1041: 5,900,000 -- ClassicChainConfig's DisposalBlock. The client returns before the explosion clause, so no bomb term is added at all
